### Dynamically Changing Layout with setPageLayout

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/guide/directory-structure/app/layouts

Illustrates how to change the page layout dynamically using the `setPageLayout` helper function. This is useful for conditional layout assignments.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
function enableCustomLayout () {
  setPageLayout('custom')
}
definePageMeta({
  layout: false,
});
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <button @click="enableCustomLayout">Update layout</button>
  </div>
</template>
```

--------------------------------

### Using a Named Layout in a Page

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/guide/directory-structure/app/layouts

Demonstrates how to assign a specific layout ('custom') to a page using `definePageMeta`. The layout name is normalized to kebab-case.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
definePageMeta({
  layout: 'custom'
})
</script>
```

--------------------------------

### Overriding Layout on Per-Page Basis

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/guide/directory-structure/app/layouts

Shows how to override the default layout for a specific page by setting `layout: false` in `definePageMeta` and then using the `<NuxtLayout>` component within the page itself.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
definePageMeta({
  layout: false,
})
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <NuxtLayout name="custom">
      <template #header> Some header template content. </template>

      The rest of the page
    </NuxtLayout>
  </div>
</template>
```

--------------------------------

### Registering a Layout with Dynamic Contents

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/kit/layout

Shows how to register a layout by providing its content directly using the `getContents` function within `addLayout`. This example registers a 'custom' layout with a header, footer, and a slot for page content.

```typescript
import { addLayout, defineNuxtModule } from '@nuxt/kit'

export default defineNuxtModule({
  setup () {
    addLayout({
      write: true,
      filename: 'my-layout.vue',
      getContents: () => `<template>
  <div>
    <header>My Header</header>
    <slot />
    <footer>My Footer</footer>
  </div>
</template>`,
    }, 'custom')
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Registering a Custom Layout with Nuxt Kit

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/kit/layout

Demonstrates how to register a custom layout using the `addLayout` utility from Nuxt Kit within a Nuxt module. It shows how to resolve template paths and assign a name to the layout.

```typescript
import { addLayout, createResolver, defineNuxtModule } from '@nuxt/kit'

export default defineNuxtModule({
  setup () {
    const { resolve } = createResolver(import.meta.url)

    addLayout({
      src: resolve('templates/custom-layout.ts'),
      filename: 'custom-layout.ts',
    }, 'custom')
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Dynamically Setting Layout in app.vue

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/guide/directory-structure/app/layouts

This example shows how to dynamically set the layout used by Nuxt in `app.vue`. The `layout` variable can be determined based on application state or API calls.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
// You might choose this based on an API call or logged-in status
const layout = "custom";
</script>

<template>
  <NuxtLayout :name="layout">
    <NuxtPage />
  </NuxtLayout>
</template>
```

--------------------------------

### Applying a Custom Layout in a Nuxt Page

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/kit/layout

Illustrates how to apply a registered custom layout ('custom') to a specific Nuxt page (`about.vue`) by using `definePageMeta` with the `layout` option.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
definePageMeta({
  layout: 'custom',
})
</script>

<template>
  <div>About Page</div>
</template>

```

--------------------------------

### Define Layout in Nuxt 3 using definePageMeta

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/migration/pages-and-layouts

Illustrates how to specify a layout for a page in Nuxt 3 using the `definePageMeta` compiler macro. Layouts are kebab-cased, so 'customLayout.vue' becomes 'custom'.

```vue
<script setup>
definePageMeta({
  layout: 'custom'
})
</script>
```

--------------------------------

### Nuxt App.vue with Layouts

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/guide/directory-structure/app/app

This snippet illustrates how to use app.vue with Nuxt's layout system. The <NuxtLayout /> component wraps <NuxtPage /> to apply defined layouts to different pages.

```vue
<template>
  <NuxtLayout>
    <NuxtPage />
  </NuxtLayout>
</template>

```

--------------------------------

### addLayout Utility

Source: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/kit/layout

Registers a template as a layout and adds it to the layouts collection. In Nuxt 2, the `error` layout could also be registered, but in Nuxt 3+, `error.vue` in the project root replaces this.

```APIDOC
## `addLayout`

### Description
Registers a template as a layout and adds it to the layouts collection.

### Method
```typescript
function addLayout(layout: NuxtTemplate | string, name: string): void
```

### Parameters

#### `layout` Parameter

- **Type**: `NuxtTemplate | string`
- **Required**: Yes
- **Description**: A template object or a string with the path to the template. If a string is provided, it will be converted to a template object with `src` set to the string value. If a template object is provided, it must have the following properties:
  
  - **`src`** (`string`, Optional): Path to the template. If `src` is not provided, `getContents` must be provided instead.
  - **`filename`** (`string`, Optional): Filename of the template. If `filename` is not provided, it will be generated from the `src` path. In this case, the `src` option is required.
  - **`dst`** (`string`, Optional): Path to the destination file. If `dst` is not provided, it will be generated from the `filename` path and nuxt `buildDir` option.
  - **`options`** (`Record<string, any>`, Optional): Options to pass to the template.
  - **`getContents`** (`(data) => string | Promise<string>`, Optional): A function that will be called with the `options` object. It should return a string or a promise that resolves to a string. If `src` is provided, this function will be ignored.
  - **`write`** (`boolean`, Optional): If set to `true`, the template will be written to the destination file. Otherwise, the template will be used only in virtual filesystem.

#### `name` Parameter

- **Type**: `string`
- **Required**: Yes
- **Description**: The name to register the layout under (e.g., `default`, `custom`, etc.).

### Example

```typescript
import { addLayout, defineNuxtModule } from '@nuxt/kit'

export default defineNuxtModule({
  setup () {
    addLayout({
      write: true,
      filename: 'my-layout.vue',
      getContents: () => `<template>
  <div>
    <header>My Header</header>
    <slot />
    <footer>My Footer</footer>
  </div>
</template>`,
    }, 'custom')
  },
})
```

### Usage in Pages

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
definePageMeta({
  layout: 'custom',
})
</script>

<template>
  <div>About Page</div>
</template>
```

### Note on Virtual Files

Due to the lack of support for virtual `.vue` files by `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, you can work around this limitation by passing `write: true` to the first argument of `addLayout`.
```

</tool-use>

Created a three-section layout for your Nuxt application.

## Created Layout Structure

1. **Created `/app/layouts/default.vue`** — Default layout with:
   - **Header section**: Named slot `header` (with optional default content)
   - **Main content section**: Default slot for page content
   - **Footer section**: Named slot `footer` with default copyright text ("© 2025 NuxtPulse. All systems operational.") in light gray

2. **Updated `/app/app.vue`** — Wrapped `<NuxtPage />` with `<NuxtLayout />` to apply the layout

## Layout Features

- Flexbox layout: `min-h-screen flex flex-col` ensures full height
- Header: `flex-shrink-0` at the top
- Main: `flex-grow` expands to fill available space
- Footer: `flex-shrink-0` at the bottom with light gray text (`text-gray-400`)

## Usage

- Pages automatically use this layout
- To use a different layout, create another layout file and specify it in pages:
  ```vue
  <script setup>
  definePageMeta({
    layout: 'other-layout-name'
  })
  </script>
  ```
- You can override header/footer content using named slots in pages:
  ```vue
  <template>
    <template #header>Custom Header</template>
    <template #footer>Custom Footer</template>
    Your page content here
  </template>
  ```

The layout is ready to use. Pages will render with the header, main content, and footer structure.
